newsitem.title: UK: BT shares hold day's gains on results.
newsitem.headline: BT shares hold day's gains on results.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications were over two percent higher on Thursday in a falling market, holding most of the day's gains triggered by favourable second-quarter and half-year figures.

BT shares touched a high of 371p before settling back to trade at 369p around midday, up 8-1/2p on the day. BT counted among London's four most-traded shares in volume of just over 16.3 million shares.
Marketmakers said the stock had continued to gain on optimistic comment from analysts following a company meeting earlier in the day.
"I think most analysts came out of today's meeting fairly optimistic about the company," one marketmaker said.
A second trader said the meeting had allayed worries about the proposed tie-up with MCI Communications.
Patrick Hickey, telecoms analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite in London said he was encouraged by the meeting.

"(BT chairman Peter) Bonfield was quite upbeat and the results were very encouraging. The bare pretax figure of 730 million stg doesn't give the entire picture. If you strip out the bits and pieces, there was progress of about 7.4 percent in the second quarter," Hickey said.

Hickey said the most positive factor was BT's inland core volume growth, which he said was up over 10 percent in the second quarter. "That growth came at a time when the cable companies are rolling out their networks but despite that, BT managed to hold the number of residential lines," he said.
Hickey said Henderson Crosthwaite recommended buying BT stock. He said he was unlikely to change that recommendation or his earnings forecasts for the full year.
